evidence.excerpt: A simulation workflow is described that takes hourly meteorological station data (dry-bulb temperature and relative humidity) as its sole external boundary condition and predicts the time-history of the dew-point margin on the coldest internal surface of a sealed outdoor enclosure. The workflow chains a thermal resistance–capacitance model of the enclosure wall with a lumped vapour mass-balance model and a local surface temperature correction derived from a short CFD pre-computation. It was applied to three years of hourly data (2021–2023) from the Rimski Šančevi meteorological station near Novi Sad for three enclosure configurations: unheated ABS 1-litre, unheated aluminium 4-litre, and aluminium 4-litre with 10 W anti-condensation heater. The workflow predicted that the unheated ABS enclosure experienced 312 condensation-onset events over three years; the unheated aluminium enclosure experienced 94, and the heated aluminium enclosure experienced zero. Predictions were validated against a 12-month data set from four instrumented enclosures deployed at the same station, with onset event counts matching to within 8 %.
